decisions.reason: As a flagship extension of the firm's core cloud messaging stack, it remains highly aligned with existing knowledge and in-house R&D, so management would be more likely to refine or bundle it than withdraw it.

The service still draws on the firm's established multichannel messaging capabilities and serves customers bridging legacy and digital workflows, but its legacy fax angle makes it more vulnerable if demand continues to fade.

Although close to the firm's fax expertise, this narrow optimization feature is the easiest to absorb into standard operations or discontinue as resources shift toward broader cloud and digital workflow offerings.
Threat protection fits the firm's secure communications positioning very well, and the firm's absorptive capacity in email security and R&D supports ongoing learning and commercial improvement.

Multi-engine virus scanning remains closely related to the firm's email infrastructure and security competencies, making retention likely even if it is increasingly packaged as part of a wider secure messaging suite.
